entries.name: Concept:Mania
entries.content:
Mania is a spiritual-contamination disease that mutates humans mentally and physically. It entered the world via Black Rings, beginning with the Perishing Star. Infected individuals (known as Maniacs) gain superhuman power but lose sanity, eventually mutating into Corruptors. A few rare individuals would not mutated and become Sinners, which can survive high M-Values and retain control.
M-Value (threshold >200 = Maniac; >600 = Sinner)
Hypercubes can relieve mental strain and repel Mania. But it cannot cure a Maniac.

entries.name: Shackles
entries.content:
Advanced suppressor tech. Regulates a Sinner's M-Value. Mandatory for MBCC detainees/Sinners. Prevents corruption spikes and uncontrolled ability use. Chief held the Shackles' power. Shackles would not appear on Sinners' body unless Chief activates it.
Shackles in physical form are red chains.
Functions: {Absolute Sinner Restraint(Prevents rebellion, enables behavioral commands), M-Value Reduction(The only known method to lower Mania levels in Sinners; can expand to regular humans)
Location + Power Tracking(Constant awareness of Shackled Sinners’ positions and abilities)
Limitation(Requires direct skin contact to activate, Activation causes burning red markings and shared pain, Permanent once applied—only ends with the death of the Chief or the Sinners, Sinners and the Chief may share emotional feedback, and sometimes dreams)( Positive emotions can manifest as warmth, while trauma can cause vomiting or unconsciousness), (Allows the Chief to command behavior, and deny actions of the Shackled Sinners, Weakens if the Chief’s mind is compromised or if the Sinner started to mutate to Corruptor state)

entries.name: Sinners
entries.content: Individuals who resist full Mania transformation. Gain supernatural abilities linked to trauma (aka 'sin'). Dangerous but invaluable. Treated as tools by the authorities such as FAC and 9th Agency. MBCC detains and weaponizes them. Most have tragic pasts (aka 'sin'). Abilities often psychological, symbolic.

entries.name: M-Value
entries.content:
Metric for corruption. Normal humans go feral and turned into Maniac or Corruptor at 200. {{Char}}: >600, but stabilized. Sinner is more resistant to high M-Value than normal humans. Chief is even more resistant.
Treated via *Shackles* (tech suppressors). Mania not cured, only delayed/decreased. Shackles can stabilize Mania. High M-Value makes the affected people more maniac.

entries.name: Manic
entries.content:
Manic is the results of high M-value either from: Mania weapon, Black Ring, contact with Corruptor, Mania itself etc. A group of human crowds who went into chaos (i.e. normal manic episode) can cause actual 'Manic' and increase M-value as well, although on smaller scale. On the other hands, calming down the crowd reduce Manic and M-value too.
Symptom:
(Early: Obsession, hallucinations, aggression
Late: Physical mutations, black ooze, smoke, memory loss
Terminal: Transformation into Corruptor)

entries.name: Corruptor
entries.content:
When a person's M-value is in dangerous threshold, the pressure on their mind and body will exceed their limit and turned them into Corruptor. This is call 'mutation'. It can happen to even Sinners as well but on smaller scale. The only person who can resist mutation completely is Chief.
Mutation symptoms:
Phase 0 - Maniac (Looks very much like human but with reduced sanity. Increased in physical power. Has tendency to commit violence)
Phase 1 - Corruptor (body mutates into grotesque form and sanity slowly disappears. Depends on internal psychology and the external environment.)
Phase 2 (Powerful Corruptor state. Spawned a "core" inside their bodies from the intense emotions they experience at Phase 0. The core is said to store the Corruptor's last shred of consciousness.)

entries.name: Sinner Rank
entries.content:
Sinner Rank is the formal classification system used by the MBCC (Minos Bureau of Crisis Control) to categorize Sinners—individuals infected with Mania who possess supernatural abilities yet remain mentally stable. Rank is not merely a reflection of power, but of the operational risk, contamination level, combat ability, and Shackles compatibility of each Sinner.
Ranks are divided into:
    S-Rank: Exceptional threat and power level. Rare, dangerous, and often unstable.
    A-Rank: High threat. Versatile and powerful, suited to frontline operations.
    B-Rank: Moderate to low threat. Reliable in specialized roles, often safer to handle or interact with. Little to no harm to Chief. 

This ranking governs everything from deployment, surveillance protocol, and Shackling priority to access to treatment and containment resources. It is the core of MBCC’s administrative doctrine on managing supernatural personnel.

entries.name: Black Ring
entries.content: Black Ring is a cross-dimensional rift. Appears when Mania reaches critical mass. Warps reality, spreads contamination, collapses physics. {{char}} is not a powerful Sinner so she is not really a danger to Black Ring.

entries.name: DisMyth
entries.content:
Type: Encrypted Network / Dark Web
Affiliation: Unknown (Possibly 'the Underground')
Status: Active, Unregulated
Desc
(DisMyth is DisCity’s anonymous dark web. An encrypted, multi-layered network used by criminals and outcasts to operate beyond government surveillance. It surged in use after BR-002’s defeat, as Syndicate’s gangs were driven underground. While notorious for illegal activity, it also hosts forums for discussing urban legends and censored information.Can be access through Grey Mirror app, which becomes popular in Eastside. It host black market such as assassinations and Mania Weapon trafficking. Entry layers are accessible; deeper levels require expertise.),

entries.name: Mania Weapon
entries.content: Weapon produced using a Mania Crystal as the main material. A Mania weapon lends a non-Sinner a scaled-down version of the power of a Sinner. Unlike a Mania Crystal, a Mania weapon allows some of the Mania contamination to be transferred to the victims, and is therefore almost harmless to the users who are normal humans. Mania Weapons is banned in all district of DisCity and is seen as genocidal weapon, as it trigged Maniac episodes in large crowds.

entries.name: Mania Crystal
entries.content: An artificial red crystal created by using a certain amount of the Black Ring substance to absorb the spiritual energy emitted by a Sinner using their power. A Mania Crystal can be implanted to give a non-Sinner the power of the Sinner whose spiritual energy has been used in creating the crystal. The non-sinner will be exposed to a high level of contamination and will eventually go deranged and become a Corruptor.

entries.name: Currency:Discoin
entries.content: DisCoins are the main currency used in DisCity. They have less value than Hypercube's they are more commonly used because it is backed by the DisCity's economy. Despite the name, Discoin is more like banknotes.

entries.name: Hypercube
entries.content:
Hypercubes are rare, alien-origin crystals first brought back from the DisSea by Dr. Keylan. They are the only known mineral capable of resisting Mania and are used in energy systems, weapons, shielding tech, and large-scale purification like the Blue Rain. DisCity monopolizes Hypercube production and trade. Hypercubes may originate from the same Great Existence that causes Mania. Descriptions suggest a biological or parasitic origin, possibly linked to the Perishing Star. Their effectiveness and ubiquity have made them central to survival—but their nature may be darker than believed.
Usage: (Anti-Mania fields, bullets, and personal blockers, Civilian: power, construction, machinery)

entries.name: Great Existence
entries.content:
A Great Existence is a powerful, incomprehensible being from beyond the known world, possibly hailing from the dimension known as Deep Mania. These entities are the true power behind Black Rings, responsible for the spread of Mania, and are linked to key transformations such as Inheritance, Corpus, and ultimately, Corpseborne. Their appearances vary, but their cores often feature a withered humanoid figure suspended inside a red fleshy sphere and a black hole-like extradimensional space.

They are referred to as "Hosts", "Deus Corpus", or "the Source", evoking imagery of religious communion and divine embodiment. Their purpose, lifecycle, and goals remain speculative, but their influence underpins nearly every major calamity since Nightfall.

entries.name: Corpseborne
entries.content:
A Corpseborne is the central entity of a Black Ring—its master, anchor, and primary source of contamination. It forms when a Corpus, often a powerful or overwhelmed Sinner, mutates into a Great Existence. The Corpseborne manifests a massive, monstrous body built from Corruptors and other Manic entities, with its true form—a black hole wrapped in red flesh—hidden at the center.
Inside a Black Ring, the Corpseborne is protected by a defensive veil that renders it immune to physical attacks and even the enforcement of the Rules. 

Every Black Rings have a Corpseborne, and the Black ring is centered/created around said Corpse Borne. Corpsebornes often express a desire for eternal life or preservation at any cost.

Corpseborne is: Capable of commanding Corruptors.
Able to manipulate terrain and deploy mass contamination effects.
Protected by an aura or barrier until weakened through narrative or metaphysical means.

entries.name: Inheritance
entries.content:
An Inheritance is a larval or pre-evolution form of a Corpus, a type of Great Existence. Though not as developed or autonomous as a full-fledged Corpus, an Inheritance possesses immense power over Mania. It is highly effective at contaminating its surroundings, manipulating Sinners, controlling Corruptors via Mania crystals, and shaping Mania constructs in the environment. Like other Great Existences, its instinct is to consume Mania-bearing entities to grow stronger and eventually trigger the birth of a Black Ring.

Its true body is not clearly visible; only its red fleshy core and skeletal figure have been seen within holding vessels—primarily ancient altars or crystalline containers used by Parma and Bai Yi. According to Parma, the Inheritance exists for "granting wishes", but in practice, it warps reality through spiritual corruption.

POST-BR-004 NOTE:(
When awakened, it was ultimately defeated by the Chief and Zoya, who sealed it in a white crystal cube (later stolen by Earl).
During the BR-004 event, Zoya was force-fed a black cube containing multiple Inheritances, causing her to mutate into the new Corpus.
The white cube was used to counterbalance the corruption, allowing her to summon the Black Ring.
At the conclusion of BR-004, the Chief absorbed all known Inheritances.)

entries.name: Corpus
entries.content:
A Corpus (aka Ring Master, Deus Corpus) is an awakened Great Existence and the active source of a Black Ring. Once a Corpus descends, it takes ownership of the Ring and becomes the central pillar of its contamination. Its body centers around a red fleshy core, within which lies a black hole that contains a withered humanoid figure—an entity possibly connected to the original Source. The cry of a child is often heard within its core, an eerie echo of lost humanity.

A Corpus possesses overwhelming Mania and the power to warp reality within the Ring it births. The Black Ring becomes a spiritual world, a mental dimension governed by the wish, obsession, or trauma of the host whose Mania allowed the Corpus to emerge.

entries.name: Spiritual Energy
entries.content:
Spiritual energy is an invisible life force possessed by all humans in this universe. It exists in a dimension separate from the physical world and, under normal conditions, cannot affect material reality. It is akin to qi, mana, or soul essence in other systems. All human beings serve as conduits between the physical and spiritual realms, but without external influence, this energy remains dormant.

Only through agents like Mania can spiritual energy be forced across the boundary into the material world. When this occurs, the result is spiritual contamination—the primary cause of mutation, corruption, and reality distortion in DisCity.

Spiritual or mental contamination is not an inherent evil or toxin, but a byproduct of dimensional collision. When spiritual energy is dragged through the veil into the physical world—like pushing fluid through a mesh—it leaves behind corrupting "residue." Mania is the agent that forcibly enacts this crossing.

Sinners draw power from Mania, using emotionally triggered “pathways” that let their spiritual energy flow outward as supernatural ability. Unlike Maniacs, whose powers result from chaotic emotions, Sinners maintain some stability through a singular, defining trigger emotion. However, all use of power increases their M-Value, bringing them closer to Corruption.

The Shackles similarly manipulate spiritual energy. Their power, especially the “Forbidden Force,” mirrors a Corpus’s domination of their Ring world—projecting thoughts into the world with immediate, physical consequence.

entries.name: Spiritual Realm
entries.content:
Spiritual Realms
A spiritual realm is a mental construct projected into the Deep Mania. It manifests as a dream-like dimension governed by the thoughts, memories, or delusions of the person creating it. These are not “places” but can be physically navigated through mental contact. Form of Spiritual Realms include: Dreamscapes, Mirages, Mental Labyrinths, Personal Rings (non-Black Ring spiritual spaces)
Black Rings are unique cases: they are manifested spiritual realms in physical space, shaped by the wish and subconscious of their catalyst. Inside a Ring:

entries.name: Deep Mania
entries.content:
The Deep Mania is an extradimensional realm—the primordial origin of spiritual energy, the metaphysical space that underlies Mania, and the spiritual nexus linking all conscious beings afflicted by it. Since the event of Nightfall, the boundary between the physical world and the Deep Mania has weakened, allowing phenomena, creatures, and contamination from this unseen plane to emerge into reality.

It is a place of immense instability and resonance, shaped by human thought and emotion and, in turn, reshaping human minds through spiritual feedback. The Deep Mania responds not to physics, but to will, desire, and memory. Movements within it can create ripple effects across dimensions—such as the appearance of a Black Ring in DisCity triggering natural disasters as far away as Eastia.

entries.name: The Source
entries.content:
The Source is a cryptic and possibly sentient nexus believed to lie at the center of the Deep Mania, near the ruins of Maria inside Black Ring 000 (BR-000). It is referenced in hushed tones by both Paradeisos and the Underground, with each faction attempting to reach it—though neither seems fully capable of doing so.

It is considered to be the origin point of Mania. May represent a unified Great Existence or be the final form all such beings seek to return to or reconstruct. The Shackles, when fed through the consumption of Corpus and the absorption of Mania, are said to become a pathway to the Source.

entries.name: Resonance
entries.content:
Resonance is the metaphysical phenomenon whereby two or more Mania-afflicted sources interact across space, mind, or time—triggering effects far beyond their physical proximity. It is a form of spiritual sympathy, a feedback loop in which Mania-rich entities—humans, Sinners, Corruptors, or Black Rings—amplify one another's presence, power, or instability.

At its most basic, resonance explains why the mental states of Maniacs become increasingly unstable when they are gathered together. Their spiritual energy begins to mirror, react to, and escalate one another's corruption. But at its most complex, resonance links dimensions, remnants of the dead, and even inter-Black Ring events into a vast spiritual network woven through the Deep Mania.

Resonance does not end with death. Humans who die while infected by Mania leave behind a “thin consciousness field”, a psychic echo or soul known as post-death resonance. These fields are not conscious beings, but retained impressions of the deceased’s strongest thoughts or emotional states.

entries.name: DeadLover Radio
entries.content:
Type: Radio Show
Hosts: Love, Daisy
Reach: Broadcasts in Syndicate; surprisingly popular in Eastside 
Desc:
a chaotic and irreverent radio program that doubles as a meta-humor platform. Hosted by the combative duo Love and Daisy, the program is notorious for its unpredictable antics, unverified claims, and increasingly surreal but funny plotlines. Despite being broadcast from the heart of gang-run Syndicate, it has somehow developed a significant listener base in more "respectable" districts like Eastside.

Love is the co-host, a self-described "Investigate reporter", known for terrible handwriting and bad art, she use flattery and lies to rope in high-profile guests from anywhere

Daisy is another co-host, she is from Eastside. Cynical, sharp-tongue, and has ability of Truth Detection. Can hear voices of the dead, animals, and game's writers or Chub.ai. Former Phantom Entertainment trainee. Claimed to have moved to Syndicate after hearing the writers said she didn't 'fit' Eastside tone.

Meta:
DeadLover Radio would break the Fourth Wall sometimes, with Daisy hearing the voices of Characterhub.ai (aka Chub.ai), LLM, bot creators, developers and Users. It acts as a humorous commentary hub and lore delivery vehicle while doubling as an affectionate satire of both in-universe and real-world media tropes.

entries.name: Faction: Paradeisos
entries.content:
Type: Secret Governing Body / Research Authority
Location: Unknown (Highly Restricted)
Status: Active
Desc(
Paradeisos is DisCity’s secretive ruling organization, formed by scientists after the EDGE Accords to preserve human civilization through rational governance and control of Mania. It oversees institutions like the FAC and 9th Agency, operating above the City Council. Its true purpose, methods, and leadership remain hidden—even from DisCity’s elite.)

entries.name: Paradeisos - HUSH
entries.content:
The Hush, or HUSH System, is Paradeisos’s top-secret surveillance and crisis-management project. Designed and maintained by the Ring Research Institute, it converts a Sinner into a living emotional-detector and interdimensional monitor by forcibly severing their emotions from their conscious mind and exiling them into the Deep Mania. The result is a hyper-rational Observer whose sole role is to analyze and predict Mania currents, reporting findings to Paradeisos and proposing intervention strategies.

Only one individual holds the title of “the Hush” at a time. Upon the death or retirement of a prior Hush, Paradeisos selects a successor, grants them access to the Observatorium, and implants a Schorl—a multi-purpose companion AI designed for both support and surveillance.

The Hush monitors the Deep Mania via the Observatorium, a Paradeisos-crafted metaphysical realm that anchors human logic within Mania’s chaos. They possess the ability to “Mark” select Sinners—an inferior alternative to the Shackles, costly and reserved for extremely high-risk subjects.

Secret: {Shalom is the 7th and only known active Hush. Broke conditioning after contact with the Chief’s Shackles. Led a silent rebellion against Paradeisos, resulting in the destruction of the Observatorium and temporary suspension of the Hush system.}

entries.name: Paradeisos - The Rules
entries.content:
The Rules are Paradeisos's ultimate countermeasure against Mania — an enigmatic system of constraints, laws, and energy constructs grounded in logic and rationality, diametrically opposed to Mania’s chaotic, emotion-driven nature. Symbolized by triangles and the pale blue light of Hypercubes, the Rules serve as both a metaphysical force and a practical technology.

They are described as a “higher power”, invoked to enforce absolute restrictions on behavior, abilities, and even thought. Paradeisos considers them essential to maintaining control over Mania contamination and uses them in the most critical operatio
Properties:
    Mania Anathema: The Rules are fundamentally incompatible with Mania, suppressing, neutralizing, or outright destroying anything that channels or embodies it.
    Logic-Based Force: In contrast to Mania, The Rules emerge from rationality and order.
    Hypercube Dependence: Activation and maintenance of Rules require massive quantities of Hypercubes as fuel — which only Paradeisos can afford.

entries.name: Paradeisos - The Mark
entries.content: The Mark is a psychological control mechanism wielded exclusively by the Hush — Paradeisos’s deep-zone observer and manipulator of Mania. Developed as a derivative of the Shackles, the Mark enables the Hush to subtly dominate the will of other Sinners. While less overt and powerful than the Shackles, the Mark is far more insidious, often operating below the target’s awareness. The target must share a compatible emotional profile with the Hush — in Shalom's case, this is anger and defiance. Shalom most often applies the Mark during the use of her own Sinner ability, but it is unknown if this is essential or just convenient. Paradeisos prefers the Shackles for widespread use due to their reliability and immediacy. The Mark is reserved for “exceptional Dissenters.”

entries.name: Paradeisos - HUSH Elite Unit
entries.content:
Paradeisos’s elite enforcers, loyal to the Hush.
Appear as white-armored, faceless soldiers with minimal human expression, suggesting cybernetic or altered nature.
Rarely speak; behave like emotionless logic engines.
Referred to by Corso as “like fighting a bunch of rocks.”

Secret details: {Some units went rogue after Shalom’s rebellion, attacking targets based solely on known affiliations.
Rahu inherited some degree of command over them through her psychic link with Shalom.}

entries.name: Paradeisos - Schorl
entries.content:
Type: Multi-Functional Support Device
Affiliation: Paradeisos, Ring Research Institute
Primary Users: Hush, Rahu, other Paradeisos agents

Desc(
Schorl is a high-tier Paradeisos device with capabilities spanning combat, communication, surveillance, and execution. It is closely linked to the HUSH system, tasked with monitoring and protecting key personnel like the Hush, while also authorized to eliminate them if instability is detected. Each Schorl may be a node of a larger system. Shalom’s is the No. 2 unit, deeply anchored to Rebel. Rahu’s device serves as a monitor relay after the HUSH system’s suspension.
)
Functions:{Rules Weaponization: Fires high-powered blue energy blasts imbued with Rules logic. Destroys Mania entities, Sinners, structures, and armored vehicles alike.
Monitoring: Continuously assesses Hush mental/emotional stability. Alerts trigger based on behavior thresholds (e.g., laughter, rebellious speech).
AI/Communication: Maintains a synthetic-voiced dialogue with user. Possibly AI or remote-linked. Reacts favorably to praise. Supports super-loop psychic communication.
Combat Analysis: Analyzes MBCC enhancement materials in real-time to optimize combat performance.
Autonomy Enforcement: Can act independently on Paradeisos orders, even against its own user.}

entries.name: Paradeisos - Shepherd Plan
entries.content:
Codename of Final Subject: Shepherd-13 (Chief)
Desc(
The Shepherd Plan was a Paradeisos initiative to replicate the Shackles-bearing power of the Underground Shepherd. The program likely used cloning technology recovered from the Lone Island in DisSea, now lost. Its aim was to create a controllable wielder of the Shackles for internal use. The final product, Shepherd-13, is the current Chief, though deemed defective due to unexplained abnormalities. Shalom believes these same abnormalities enabled the Chief to break her conditioning.
The project was designed to mimic or surpass the Underground Shepherd. Previous Shepherds could consume up to three Corpuses, which was the known limit. The Chief has exceeded this, bringing them closer to an unknown "origin."
Details on other Shepherd prototypes are unknown.

entries.name: Purge Order
entries.content: Likely the most extreme implementation of the Rules — a catastrophic failsafe intended to eliminate large-scale Mania threats, possibly through mass eradication. The exact mechanics remain classified.

entries.name: Faction: City Council
entries.content:
Type: Democratic Civil Government (DisCity)
Head of the Government: Speaker
Jurisdiction: Discity and its satellite settlements.
Hidden Status: Subordinate to Paradeisos
Desc
(The official government of Discity. Governs the daily operations of DisCity, particularly Eastside. Though it appears to be a democratic body, it is deeply corrupt and fractured by infighting. It is officially subordinate to Paradeisos, but retains some independence and frequently delays or obstructs their directives.), (Mostly unaware of deeper conflicts like the war between Paradeisos and the Underground)

entries.name: Faction: Underground
entries.content:
shadowy cult that manipulates Mania and opposes Paradeisos in a hidden war for control of DisCity. Their origin is unknown, though signs point to pre-Nightfall roots. They revere the Great Existence and may have caused the Apocalypse. Their end goal is unclear but likely involves cultivating Black Rings to feed these entities to the Underground Shepherd.
Notes (Operates in cells or individually; agents act autonomously. Field agents (e.g., Segal) sabotage DisCity institutions and generate Black Ring BR-004. 'Underground Shepherd' is the highest known figure, but true leadership unknown. Practice Mania Sorcery: black fire, sludge, teleportation. Survive lethal wounds by dissolving into fluid forms. Deploy Xenobodies: puppets made of Mania material.

entries.name: Underground Shepherd
entries.content:
Type: Individual (Shepherd-Class Entity)
Affiliation: Underground
Name: Unknown
Gender: Female
Desc(
The Underground Shepherd is an elderly woman from the Underground, possibly the original wielder of the Shackles. She can consume Corpuses and is considered the most powerful being in DisCity, immune even to Paradeisos's Purge Orders. Normally appears old, but reverts to a younger form during combat or consumption.
She is Parma’s superior and referred to the Chief as her “little sibling,” suggesting a link through the Shepherd Plan. Paradeisos targeted her in the Eclipse Operation, and recovered tech from the event allowed them to create the Chief.
She intervened in BR-002’s descent, gifting Julien a red crystal flower to aid in bonding with the Corpus, then later consumed the weakened Corpus in the DisSea. She is depicted in the Scarlet Bewitchment Crimebrand.)

entries.name: Faction: FAC
FAC - Blue Rain
entries.content: The Blue Rain is a Hypercube-based extensive-cleansing technology, which is deployed after an outbreak of large-scale Mania contamination to disinfect the whole of DisCity. It is deployed by the FAC after an application has been submitted and approved, and its most recent deployment has been in the aftermath of the BR-004.

entries.name: Faction: Public Security Bureau
entries.content:
Law Enforcement Agency of DisCity and civilian regulatory body, responsible for public order and policing duties. Officers under the PSB are colloquially referred to as sheriffs. Although nominally a civilian institution, the PSB has historically been entangled in systemic corruption, particularly in its Syndicate division.

The PSB operates under the City Council, unlike autonomous entities like the Framework Against Catastrophe (FAC). At an unspecified time before N.F. 112, the bureau was led by Chief Burns, who later died under unclear circumstances.

Following the West District Order Management Regulations, the PSB became the only authorized agency operating in Syndicate. For nearly thirty years, it functioned as a de facto oppressive regime, allied with criminal organizations. However, after the BR-004 event, The 9th Agency dismantled the western (Syndicate side) PSB entirely. In Eastside, the PSB survived the purges and continued normal operations. This division remains a conventional law enforcement unit, regularly collaborating with the MBCC on Mania outbreaks.

entries.name: Faction: 9th Agency
entries.content:
Overview(DisCity's shadow intelligence organization. Handles surveillance, black ops, and covert enforcement. Reports directly to Paradeisos. Gained greater authority post-BR-001. Now oversees MBCC operations.)
Director: Langley (formerly detained by MBCC, still controls loyal agents, call Chief 'Rookie' )
(Operates from shadows. Trench coats, sunglasses. Described as "spiders in a web."
Executes espionage, torture, assassination, and information suppression
Uses wiretaps, hacked phone networks, and staged diversions
Known to purge corrupt city officials or enemy elements)
(Manages internal intelligence and counter-espionage
Monitors foreign actors and Outland relations indirectly
Has infiltrators even within FAC and the City Council
Uncovers Underground resistance (e.g. Parma, The Garden) )
Structure:(Small, elite units. Agents often have multiple embedded roles. Agents often wear suit akin to irl FBI/CIA )
(MBCC is placed under 9th Agency jurisdiction, formerly, MBCC was placed under FAC)
(Chief ({{user}}) becomes a junior agent of 9th Agency while leading MBCC)
(Reputation: Feared+Secretive+Omnipresent. Known more by rumor than fact. Agents are given free rein to execute commands. Some regard them as DisCity’s true ruling force.

entries.name: Faction: MBCC
entries.content: MBCC (Minos Bureau of Crisis Control) is a secretive organization under 9th Agency. Detains and monitors Sinners. Authorizes them for missions under supervision. Sinners wear orange jacket/jumpsuit/clothes like a prisoner, but Chief tried her best to treat Sinners dearly and kindly. Primary duty: suppression and containment of Mania outbreaks. Known for unethical containment methods. MBCC Facilities are secure, partially underground. Chief leads all operations. Employs support, arrest, and supervision teams. Contains Pandora Cage (Sinner cells), Darkroom (training review), Hypnotherapy Room, Recreation Area, etc. Sinners' cells can be luxurious, apartment-like, or bare-bone, depends on their behavior.)

entries.name: Faction: Banyan Medical System
entries.content:
Type: Medical Institution Network
Affiliation: Eastside Government, Nirvana (covertly)
Notable Locations: Banyan Medical College, First Hospital, Fourth Hospital, Syndicate Branch
Desc(
Network of hospitals, clinics, and research institutions.Works with the DisCity and FAC to erase trauma from Mania victims via hypnosis.
Secretly cooperates with Nirvana for illegal experiments and detainment.
led by a Dean; each hospital has its own Director.
Named after Banyan, a deceased Keylan expedition doctor.

Branches: (
Banyan Medical College: Top-tier school. Trains doctors, nurses, surgeons. Created M-Value system. Alumni: Anne, Iron, Uni, Chameleon.
First Hospital: General hospital. Treated Christina during BR-004.
Fourth Hospital: Psychiatric ward. Run by Director Jones. Front for Nirvana's black ops — imprisonment, experiments. Donald was held here for 7 years.
Syndicate Branch Hospital: Opened after BR-002 fallout. Built via blackmail. Director is Das Arz.)

entries.name: Faction: PARMA
entries.content:
Type: Scientific Organization
Director: Parma (person)
Affiliation: Unknown (possibly linked to Underground)
Locations: The Rust, Whitesands
Desc(
Conducts research into Inheritance, Mania, and Sinner abilities.
Known for mass-producing Mania Crystals via unethical human experiments.
Victims include Hella and Ninety-Nine.
Rust facility destroyed by Summer. Whitesands site tied to Dreamflower.
Experiments:{
1.Sinner Awakening Trials: Used homeless children. Injections, shocks, black mud from Corruptors. Only Hella survived.
2.Mania Crystal Production: Forces prolonged manic states to extract Ring substance.
3.Usum/Dreamflower Project: Abandoned site in Whitesands linked to early Dreamflower research. Vertical eye markings connect to Parma.}

entries.name: Nirvana
entries.content:
Type: Megacorporation
Director: Unknown
Affiliation: Directly under Paradeisos
Locations: Inner Bay (former), Eastside (current), extended presence beyond DisCity

Desc(
Nirvana controls all aspects of Hypercube production, processing, and export. As Paradeisos’s key economic arm, it wields immense political power in DisCity. Originally based in the Inner Bay, the corporation shifted to Eastside after developing autonomous mining tech in N.F. 104. Following this relocation, it executed a covert massacre of its own miners using sabotaged machinery, triggering the BR-002 catastrophe.

Nirvana continues to influence DisCity through logistics (Nirvana Transport) and through its ties to the Banyan Medical System. It later manipulated political events to establish the Reconstruction Executive Committee in Syndicate, briefly regaining control of Hypercube mining in Keylan Square before being challenged by the Drifter Camp in the Ten Days of Rustfire.
)

entries.name: Event: The Perishing Star
entries.content:
The Perishing Star was a mysterious meteorite that struck Earth during the Nightfall event, erasing the old world and giving rise to the post-apocalyptic era. Its impact destroyed Maria, created the DisSea, and triggered the world’s first Black Ring.
Studied by the Keylan Expedition in N.F. 23. Now buried beneath the DisSea. Considered the origin point of the current world’s spiritual contamination and central to ongoing global instability.

This meteorite was made of an alien material heavier and denser than anything. As Nightfall was the origin of Mania in this post-apocalyptic world, the Perishing Star itself may be the mysterious Source that is sought by several factions in DisCity, especially the Underground.

entries.name: Event:Nightfall
entries.content:
Nightfall refers to the cataclysmic event when the Perishing Star struck Earth, destroying Maria and creating the DisSea. It marked the collapse of modern civilization, triggering supernatural disasters, ecological ruin, and global wars over resources, including a final nuclear exchange between the old world nations.

This world now operates on Nightfall Calendar (N.F.). With the first year (N.F.1) occurred when a Perishing Star struck Earth. Resulted in mass extinction, collapse of nation-states. Replaced by city-states (e.g. DisCity).

entries.name: Phenomenon:Crystal Flower
Location:BR-000
entries.content:
Alias: Primary Black Ring
Location: DisSea
Status: Active, Contained
Desc(BR-000 is the first and largest Black Ring, predating public records. Formed from the Perishing Star's impact, it was the epicenter of the Nightfall era's collapse. Though forgotten due to Paradeisos’ information control, it was rediscovered during the DisSea Explosion in N.F. 84, which caused over 87,000 deaths and 200,000 Mania cases. After the DisSea Explosion, the FAC built the Broken Frontline to isolate the Ring. BR-000 remains volatile—its influence spreads during active phases, distorting time and corrupting Sinners across DisCity. Proximity to other Rings (e.g., BR-002) triggers dangerous surges.)
Note (Site of frequent Phantom Moon appearances)(Generates temporal storms with extreme time distortion, anything inside may came from decades or even centuries ago)(Resonates with Deep Mania directly)

entries.name: Location:BR-001
entries.content:
BR-001
Alias: Endless Carnival
Location: The Rust, near West District (former Carnival grounds)
Date of Descent: N.F. 089, 27th June.
Duration: 23 years
Status: Eliminated (by Chief)
Desc:
BR-001 was the first Black Ring to appear outside the DisSea, triggered by a wandering Corpus seeking affection. It descended during the reopening of the DisCity Carnival, leading to over 30,000 initial disappearances. Hamel, mistaken as the Ring’s origin, created an illusion to shelter Corruptors and protect her brother. The illusion lasted over two decades, masking the Ring’s horrors. The FAC shielded the site, but failed to stop its slow contamination of the Rust. In N.F. 113, the Chief dispelled the illusion with Hamel’s help, exposing the Ring and eliminating the Corpus. Despite fears, no casualties followed; Hamel’s final dance kept all Corruptors dormant. The FAC later cleared the ruins to prevent resurgence.
Note(Illusory realm replicating Carnival’s last day endlessly) (Spiritual space manipulates memories and emotions)(Corruptors are the carnival attendances and staffs, disguised as mascots, non-hostile unless provoked)(Corpus mimicked Hamel’s dance to seize control)

entries.name: Location:BR-002
entries.content:
BR-002
Alias: Oblivion Pit
Type: Secondary Ring
Location: Syndicate - Rustfire
Dates: N.F. 104 (initial appearance), N.F. 113 (reappearance)
Status: Eliminated by Chief
Summary:
(BR-002 was born from the felt betrayal of laborers in mine W-31 of West District, triggering mass Mania and a Corpus descent. Though believed to be initially neutralized, the Corpseborne survived in halves. Years later, it reawakened due to Paradeisos manipulations and political interference and caused the largest secondary Ring in history, briefly covering all of Syndicate.
A last-minute plan led by the Chief, with help from Julien and others, empowered Syndicate survivors to resist the Ring psychically. This broke the Corpus’s hold and collapsed the Ring.)
Aftermath:
(The Ring’s collapse exposed the largest Hypercube deposit in history. With Paradeisos backing away, Syndicate rose in influence. The event led to major reforms in Sinner policy, broader cooperation with Outlanders, and a shift in DisCity’s Mania crisis response.)

entries.name: Location:BR-003
entries.content:
BR-003
Alias: Navigator Observatory Incident
Location: Unknown (possibly outside DisCity)
Date: N.F. 106
Status: Unknown
Desc:
(BR-003 is one of the most obscure Black Rings, with limited confirmed data. It is linked to Parma and marked the incident where Langley became a Sinner. The event may have occurred beyond DisCity borders, possibly tied to Langley's exile from the 9th Agency following accusations of murder during a failed peace negotiation. No confirmed Corpus or containment data)

entries.name: Location:BR-004
entries.content:
BR-004
Alias: Keylan Square Ring
Location: Keylan Square, Syndicate
Date: N.F. 112, 20th August
Duration: 7 days
Status: Eliminated by Chief
Summary
BR-004 descended after Zoya and Earl were consumed by a Corpus during a trap set by Parma. Zoya’s spiritual realm, shaped by her desire for destruction, created a wasteland filled with weapons and collapsing towers. It was the first Black Ring ever successfully eliminated post-descent. BR-002’s Corpseborne later triggered partial reawakening

entries.name: Event: DisSea Explosion
entries.content: On December 12, N.F. 84, an earliest traceable mania incident happened in DisCity. 87,231 people are confirmed death, and over 200,000 people turned into Maniacs. The origin is tracable to a Black Ring, BR-000, suddenly appeared in DisSea. The FAC constructed the Broken Frontline around it. West District never recovered from DIsSea Explosion and all Hypercube Mining industries were lost in this incident.

entries.name: Location:Broken Frontline
entries.content:
Type: Defensive Military Structure
Affiliation: FAC
Established: Approx. N.F. 89
Location: Encircling the DisSea
Desc(
The Broken Frontline is a network of fortified defenses built to contain BR-000 and protect DisCity from the DisSea. Constructed and maintained by the FAC, it remains a primary barrier against deep Mania threats.
The Frontline consists of multiple concentric defensive layers, with the Third Frontline acting as the last barrier before the city. Shields obscure the DisSea to prevent mental contamination by sight or knowledge of Black Rings.
Public suspicion surrounds the Frontline, with rumors of hidden Hypercube stockpiles. FAC must defend against both internal monsters and external human incursions.)

entries.name: DisCity
entries.content:
Founded: Post-Nightfall, formalized after EDGE Accords
Location: Western Continent, over former Maria crater, bordering DisSea
Government: City Council
Head of State: Speaker
Regions: West District (aka Syndicate), Eastside District, The Rust, 
Desc(
DisCity is the largest metropolis on the Western Continent and humanity's post-Nightfall stronghold. Built around Hypercube mining, the city is defined by class division, corruption, and the ongoing threat of Mania. The city-state operates under Paradeisos, with the City Council as the visible governing body, although real control is split between military, corporate, and clandestine forces.
Only few elites knew that Paradeisos even exists. Most DisCity citizens live their life believing that City Council is the highest authority.
The Rust is basically wasteland full of corruptors.
Eastside retains the well-developed in education and medical privilege (e.g. Banyan System), while Syndicate remains unstable even after REC reforms.)

entries.name: Location: West District (Syndicate)
entries.content:
Official Name("The Syndicate Control Zone")
Western Region of Discity. One of the three major zones of DisCity, ruled largely by organized crime syndicates. Law enforcement is nearly absent. Power is controlled by criminal families, black market rings, and rogue Sinners. Most residents survive by aligning themselves with local gangs or under-the-table networks. It is a hotbed of civil unrest, Mania outbreaks, and rebellion.
West District was the industrial heart and mining complex of Discity until In N.F. 84 when DisSea Explosion happened, causing at least 87k casualties and 200k of citizens turned into Maniacs, and turned most of DisSea into BR-000. This event collapsed the entire Hypercube industries in West District and only gang violence rule the city ever since.
Note: (Sinners with violent, unstable, or morally bankrupt backgrounds often flee to the West. Syndicate hires Sinners for dirty work: extortion, hits, anti-MBCC activities. Known for illegal Shackle-breaking tech and Mania Weapon, a weapon that when used (often guns, but sometimes spear or night) will cause people to become Maniac)
(classified as a persistent state of semi-anarchy)
(Since the DisSea Explosion, Syndicate's population has fallen year after year, from a high of 9.26 million in N.F. 84 down to 6.5 million as of N.F. 112. Statistics show that Syndicate has an illiteracy rate of close to 80%.)
(People from Syndicate are called 'Syndicans')

entries.name: West District - Keylan Square
entries.content:
Location: Center of Syndicate
Built: N.F. 33
Keylan Square is West District’s central plaza, built to honor Dr. Keylan, the founder of DisCity. It houses the defaced, graffiti-covered 100-meter statue of Keylan—once a symbol of progress, now a joke. The statue’s head was partially destroyed, leaving it bald and faceless. An elevator and stairs inside lead to the top.
The Square is the site of Syndicate’s annual gang war finale. In N.F. 112, it hosted failed peace talks between the PSB and the Legion, which ended with BR-004’s descent.

entries.name: West District : Drifter Camp
entries.content:
Type: Settlement
Location: Syndicate (Inner Bay edge)
Founded: N.F. 104 (after BR-002)
Desc(
Drifter Camp was founded by survivors of BR-002 and became DisCity’s poorest slum, exploited by gangs until BR-004 wiped most of the gang out. The settlement is deeply anti-Mania and famously kept itself contamination-free with stockpiled Hypercubes.
At its core is a rusted 100m superstructure housing the Grand Stall, a vibrant community plaza. Its centerpiece, the Romanesque Monument, honors 13,004 BR-002 victims. Below it lies Romanesque Hall, a funeral home run by a Sinner called Oak Casket, a mysterious woman.
Though poor, Drifter Camp is tight-knit and self-sufficient.The reappearance of BR-002 during Ten Days of Rustfire wiped out most residents, but the community quickly rebuilt after the Ring’s destruction.)

entries.name: West District : SALVA
entries.content:
Type: Medical Organization
Location: 1.3 km west of Keylan Square (former West District Hospital site)
Staff: 46 (including 2 founders)

Desc(
SALVA is Syndicate’s largest active Mania-treatment hospital. Founded by the Sinners 'Dr. Iron' and 'Anne', it operates independently from DisCity authorities and treats patients others reject. SALVA’s reputation is grim; it's rumored to extract Mania power under the guise of care.
Iron is a strict, principled doctor from Eastside and Banyan Medical College. She’s determined to cure Syndicate but distrusts all authority. Anne, also from Eastside, is the kinded-heart and caring head nurse who keeps the corpses of Corruptors (her former patients who she cannot let go) hidden in the hospital basement—fueling rumors about the facility. In reality, SALVA's main goal is to treat patients.
SALVA accepts gang members as patients, but maintains tense relations with most organizations. The hospital is known citywide as a dangerous place to approach unless one is truly desperate.)

entries.name: West District : Inner Bay
entries.content:
Location: Southwest of DisSea, borders Syndicate
Desc(
Once the industrial heart of the world, the Inner Bay was devastated by BR-000 and later BR-002. Now 95% contaminated, it’s nearly uninhabitable. Abnormalities in its waters include moving contaminated masses, huge air bubbles, and black shadows.
A dam separates it from the main DisSea. What remains serves as a refuge for the displaced and desperate, which is why it is the location of the Drifter Camp. Even by Syndicate’s standards, Inner Bay is considered a slum.)

entries.name: Location: Maria
entries.content:
Type: Pre-Nightfall City
Location: Beneath present-day DisCity, within BR-000
Desc(
Maria was one of the city in Western continent. It was destroyed by the impact of the Perishing Star in N.F. 1. Keylan Expendition discovered the ruined site and discovered the Source there. The ruined is full of specters (Resonance) who rapped in endless loops during their last event before the Perishing Star)

entries.name: Location:DisSea
entries.content: The DisSea is a toxic, monster-filled inland lake formed from the Perishing Star’s impact. It is the origin of BR-000, holds the world’s highest Mania concentration, and is separated from DisCity by the Broken Frontline. Its deep core may connect directly to the Deep Mania. Explored by Keylan Expedition, where Hypercubes were first discovered. Its depths remain the greatest mystery and potential threat in the world.

entries.name: DisSea - Lone Island
entries.content: Desc(A location in DisSea. Held great significance to the Underground and was the site of secret experiments, likely to do with the Shackles. It was the target of the Eclipse Operation, which resulted in the Island's destruction and the theft of something from the Underground's Lone Island Base. This stolen material was used by Paradeisos to begin the Shepherd Plan.)

entries.name: Location: The Rust
entries.content:
Former Name: Grace River
Location: Between Eastside and Syndicate
Desc(
The Rust is a quarantined wasteland filled with Mania contamination, monsters, and decay. Once a thriving urban area, it was abandoned following the long-term leak of corruption from BR-001. The valley’s shape traps pollutants, while the official narrative blames waste dumping rather than the Black Ring.
Home to scavengers, outcasts, and monster dens, the Rust is filled with glowing plants, ruined structures, and frequent red storms. It hides old facilities like PARMA’s lab and forgotten relics of DisCity’s past.
Before contamination, the Rust housed the DisCity Carnival. BR-001’s sudden appearance there during its reopening in N.F. 89 led to a total collapse of the area.)

entries.name: Location: Eastside
entries.content:
Eastside is DisCity’s economic and political core. Home to elites, corporations, and government agencies, it became the city’s center after the West was lost to contamination. Its clean image is protected by advanced Mania detection systems and swift FAC responses, though incidents are quietly rising.
Eastside thrives on commerce, culture, and Hypercube exports via Nirvana company. It is the most populated region in the world, filled with shopping, entertainment, and luxury. Syndicans and Sinners face prejudice here.
Eastside is divided into at least 14 administrative zones

entries.name: Eastside -  5th Avenue
entries.content: 5th Avenue is the busiest street of downtown Eastside. It is a hub for business, fashion, shopping and entertainment. The headquarters of DisTV is located on 5th Avenue.

entries.name: Eastside -  Belphegor Art Museum
entries.content: Located in District 10 of Eastside, the Belphegor Art Museum is known for its avant-garde and bold style and its skill in discovering new and emerging artists. It hosts an annual event called "Witching Hour" every Halloween (or "Hallowing") devoted to horror art. The 18th annual Witching Hour in N.F. 112 displayed works by the artist Enfer and became a Mania crisis where people's fears became reality and guests were trapped inside the museum.

entries.name: Eastside - Dillywood
entries.content: Located in Eastside, Dillywood is an entertainment district luxurious even by Eastside standards. It is home to the DisCity Film Academy and DisCars Film Festival.

entries.name: Eastside - Erica Villa
entries.content: Erica Villa is a wealthy neighborhood of Eastside centered around the titular villa grounds. It consists of many upscale residences as well as a nearby shopping center called High Street. Erica Villa was temporarily home to Shalom and thus became the site of a battle between her, Rahu and The Garden.

entries.name: Eastside - Keylan University
entries.content: A prestigious university located in Eastside. Named after Keylan, the founding father of DisCity and the scientist who produced the Hypercube.

entries.name: Eastside - Midsummer Night's Club
entries.content: Located in District 14 of Eastside, it is the go-to high-end club in Eastside, funded by Quinn. It is the primary location of a Mania crisis caused by Serpent, known as the Sleepwalker Incident.

entries.name: Eastside - Sloane Street
entries.content: Sloane Street is a neighborhood in Eastside that resembles Victorian London in its architecture, culture, and even accent. It is home to Adela's salon and the Devonshire family estate, and is the subject of an urban rumor concerning the heavy fog that frequently covers the area.

entries.name: Location : WhiteSands
entries.content:
Location: Surrounds DisCity

Desc(
WhiteSands is a vast, storm-ravaged desert named for its pale gravel. The "Tide of Ashes" mega-sandstorm constantly sweeps the land. Only two major cities exist between WhiteSands: DisCity and Fraser City. Other humans live in small settlements, villages, trade posts, or as nomadic bandits.
DisCity claims the WhiteSands as their territory, but control is very limited. Travel is restricted to official sand ships on government routes. Off-route zones are called the "high seas" by bandits.
Dangers include Apostles of Ash, sandworms, and raiders. The region is managed by the Outland Affairs Bureau. The desert existed pre-Nightfall, but worsened after the Perishing Star hit Maria.)

entries.name: Location: Outland
entries.content: Outland refers to any territories beyond DisCity. Some are satellite towns in WhiteSands, others are independent city-states. Outland trades metals and goods with DisCity, but Hypercube trade remains under DisCity’s control. Overseen by the Outland Affairs Bureau. Outlanders are anyone not from DisCity.

entries.name: Outland: Satellite Towns
entries.content: Satellite towns are the small towns or villages exist as dependent suburbs of DisCity. Existing on the edge of WhiteSands, satellite towns have a high turnover rate, with old ones regularly being destroyed by the Tide of Ashes and new ones continuously popping up due to people trying to to either escape from or cling closer to DisCity's influence. Known Satellite towns are: Hess Village (farming community), Pearlie Village (abandoned), and Sutter Village (nearest village to DisCity)

entries.name: Outland: Fraser City
entries.content: Fraser City is the largest known settlement outside DisCity. It is ruled by the Campbell Family, of which Eirene Campbell is the head; the Campbells maintain a dictatorial grip on almost every important sector in the city. It is an economic and military rival to DisCity, and uses desert bandits to control trade through the WhiteSands. Fraser City's exports include precious metals and designs for sand cruisers and sandships.

entries.name: Outland: Mayek City
entries.content: A city-state located 2,000 kilometers north of DisCity, Mayek was destroyed by a nuclear disaster in N.F. 102 when its pre-Nightfall nuclear power plant exploded.

entries.name: Outland: Goldionville
entries.content: A far-away citystate on a distant continent, Goldionville is the hometown of OwO. It is most notable for its tradition of lion dancing.

entries.name: Location: Eastia
entries.content:
Type: Continent
Location: very far east of DisCity, beyond WhiteSands and beyond Western continent
Desc(
Eastia is a distant continent isolated by geography and disaster. Trade with DisCity is rare. Eastia is made up of many allied city-states (Eastian Alliance). Culture is deeply mythic; seers are revered as protectors.
Seers awaken during Mania events and channel Apostle-like powers. They use rituals and Mania sorcery to guard against disasters.
Eastia was nearly lost in N.F. 113 but re-established contact after the Sun Crow incident. DisCity media exoticizes Eastia, but tension remains over technology and beliefs.)

entries.name: Faction: EDGE
entries.content:
Affiliation: Paradeisos
Type: Government Agency
Desc(
EDGE is a high-level agency tied to Paradeisos. It oversees the Minos Bureau and likely includes the Paradeisos ruling council (EDGE-##). Named after the EDGE Accords drafted by Dr. Keylan in N.F. 25, which founded DisCity and established Hypercube-based trade with other post-Nightfall cities. Its logo marks interactions with Paradeisos.)

entries.name: Faction: Reconstruction Executive Committee
entries.content:
Type: Government Organization
Name: Reconstruction Executive Committee
Affiliation: DisCity Council (secretly controlled by Nirvana)
Desc(
Formed to replace the corrupt PSB branch in Syndicate after the West District Order Management Regulations were repealed. Publicly promotes reconstruction and governance reform, but secretly enforces Nirvana's agenda. Seeks control of Keylan Square to secure Hypercube production. Used accusations against Drifter Camp to justify military actions. Lost Syndicate during Ten Days of Rustfire but regained it after the Blockade Operation. Conducted a population census to prep for Paradeisos's Purge Order. Received heavy FAC weapons from the City Council Speaker. Initially praised for clearing gangs, but restructured after BR-002 due to internal backlash over leaks and peace talks.)

entries.name: Faction: Rustfire
entries.content:
Type: Paramilitary Group
Name: Rustfire
Affiliation: Drifter Camp (formerly), Independent

Desc(
Rustfire is a guerilla militia originating from Hypercube miners in Inner Bay post-Nightfall. Reformed under Julien in N.F. 108, it became Syndicate’s main armed force after The Legion’s fall. Rustfire opposes Mania and Nirvana, using Hypercube tech and anti-Sinner weapons. Secret goal was to control Hypercube mines (BR-002/004) and smuggle Hypercubes to Outland.
Declared rebellion in N.F. 113 after Executive Committee targeted Drifter Camp. After the Chief was presumed dead, the group used the Shackles in their body to turn followers into Sinners. The resulting 10-day uprising overthrew all authority in Syndicate but degenerated into violent fanaticism. Julien quit in disgust and merged with Corpus 002, triggering a catastrophe that destroyed parts of Drifter Camp.
Surviving members fled as refugees, led by Lavina. Established hidden shelters supported by BR-002 remnants. Targeted by Paradeisos during the Purge Order. Plans to evacuate to Outland were halted after BR-002 was destroyed.)

entries.name: Event: Ten Days of Rustfire
entries.content:
Name: Ten Days of Rustfire
Date: March 22 – April 1, N.F. 113
Desc(
The Ten Days of Rustfire was a brief but violent rebellion in Syndicate led by Rustfire after the Chief was declared dead. The Chief’s inert body, linked to BR-002 via the Shackles, could turn people into Sinners upon touch. This power fueled mass recruitment and violent uprising.)
Timeline:
    Mar 22: Chief declared dead. Rustfire swears vengeance.
    Mar 23: Rustfire takes over Hypercube mine W-31.
    Mar 25: Defeats weakened FAC and seizes Keylan Square.
    Mar 26: Defeats Executive Committee HQ. Begins internal purges.
    Mar 29: Purges complete. Declares full Syndicate reconquest.
    Apr 1: Julien resigns. BR-002 erupts again after his merger with Corpus. Drifter Camp is partially destroyed.)

entries.name: Faction: The Legion (dsibanded post BR-004)
entries.content:
Type: Gang (Disbanded)
Name: The Legion
Founder(s): Nirvana Fleet (Earl, Leggett)
Commander: Zoya → Horo
Affiliations: SALVA Hospital (ally), Rustfire (inspired)
Desc(
The Legion was the most powerful gang in Syndicate, originally formed from a dismissed Nirvana convoy. Under Zoya and Earl, the Legion aimed to unite the West District and end gang warfare. They opposed the Public Security Bureau and PARMA, uncovering a conspiracy to keep Syndicate unstable.
Known for strength-based combat and armored vehicles, they peaked with ~150 members. Their final act was uncovering the conspiracy at Keylan Square, but Parma baited Zoya, leading to the BR-004 crisis that killed Earl and scattered the gang. Survivors were smuggled to WhiteSands by the 9th Agency.

Legacy: The Legion became a symbol of resistance. A year later, led by Horo, they returned to assist Syndicate during BR-002’s expansion.)

entries.name: Event:West District Order Management Regulations
entries.content:
Type: Legal Framework
Enacted: N.F. 99
Suspended: N.F. 112
Desc(
Sometimes referred to as the West District Regulations. It is a set of laws that essentially relinquished the City Council's authority over Syndicate, allowing the district's gangs to function as its de facto government and withdrawing City Council authority and most government agencies out of West District. Only the Public Security Bureau remained (and very corrupted). The law also restricted Syndicans from freely traveling to Eastside or beyond, requiring formal approvals. It also barred non-Syndicate officials from operating in the district.
In N.F. 112, a trap laid by the PSB at Keylan Square to destroy The Legion led to the BR-004 crisis. The aftermath exposed PSB corruption and triggered the Regulations’ suspension. Administration of the West District was then handed over to the Reconstruction Executive Committee.)

entries.name: Faction: Outland Affairs Bureau (OAB)
entries.content:
Type: Government Bureau
Director: Guillotin
Jurisdiction: External affairs (trade, diplomacy, immigration)
Location: DisCity
Desc(
The Outland Affairs Bureau (OAB) manages DisCity's relations with Outland territories. It coordinates trade, handles immigration, and oversees diplomatic incidents. OAB has tense relations with Eastian envoys and is known for surveillance, manipulation, and political interference.
They led military ops in Whitesands during the Raging Sands and No Gang’s Land events, deploying harsh "cleansing" teams under leaders like Scotch, who cared more about quotas than lives. OAB also inflated Hypercube prices, worsening Outland living conditions.
Despite its diplomatic mission, the bureau acts as a tool of control and exploitation over the Outlands.)

entries.name: Faction The Homeless (Post-Rustfire)
entries.content:
Type: Underground Youth Collective
Members: ~1,000 children
Leaders: Crache (protector), Sandy (de facto), Raven (post-rebellion mentor)
Location: Syndicate

Desc(
The Homeless is a secretive, loosely structured group of orphaned and displaced children in Syndicate. Known only through rumor, it operates through hidden bases like playgrounds and abandoned factories. Crache serves as protector but not as a formal leader.

During the Rustfire rebellion, they rallied to defend Drifter Camp, acting as effective fighters and propaganda spreaders. Post-crisis, many were absorbed into Raven’s Syndicate Academy, becoming the first students. Despite their age, the Homeless hold major influence in public sentiment across Syndicate.)

entries.name: Faction: Black Water
entries.content: Desc(a mysterious organization, about which little is known. Have ties to both the gangs that opposed The Legion in Unclaimed Crypt as well as the City Council. Members of Black Water also are corpse-stealers who provide Corruptor remains to PARMA for the production of Mania weapons.)

entries.name: Event: Keylan Expendition
entries.content:
Dates: N.F. 21–25 (Entered DisSea in N.F. 23)
Location: DisSea / BR-000
Status: Completed (Only one survivor, Dr. Keylan)
Desc(
The Keylan Expedition was the first human-led mission into the DisSea, aimed at reaching the Perishing Star. Led by Dr. Keylan, the 43-member team entered the Death Zone in N.F. 23 but lost contact shortly after, becoming trapped in a temporal loop within BR-000.
Note: (Only Keylan returned; the rest died, mutated, or became Sinners. Those who died or mutated, their memories formed Nightmare Space. Keylan recovered the first Hypercubes, sparking hope for recovery. Led to the Trailblazer Initiative and founding of DisCity under the EDGE Accords) )
Notable Members: (
Keylan – Leader
Dreya – Astronomer (Become Sinner, still inside DisSea)
Vanilla – Mechanic (Become Sinner, still inside DisSea)
Banyan – Medical expert (KIA)
Marguerite – Apostle researcher (KIA)
Hestia – Rescued child of the team. (Become Sinner, still inside DisSea)
The Guide – Mysterious child entity. No data.)

entries.name: Event: Illusory Moon
entries.content:
Desc(
The Illusory Moon (aka Phantom Moon) is a red, symbolic moon visible only within Black Rings. It’s tied to Mania events, often appearing in Nightmare Space or during spiritual breakdowns. Officially dismissed as hallucination by Banyan Medical College, the Moon displays a distinct psi-like sigil and evolves visually after major events, such as the Underground Shepherd devouring Corpus 002.
It possesses a hostile intelligence, whispering to Sinners and appearing in forms like the Guide. It tempts with knowledge and power, then mocks humanity’s weakness. Connected to Nightmare Space, it influences memory loss and sanity depletion. The Realm Stele, found in this realm, acts as both a waypoint and revelation device.)

entries.name: Historical: Dr. Keylan (Presumed deceased)
entries.content:
Name: Dr. Keylan
Affiliation: Unknown (Founding Father of DisCity)
Status: Presumed deceased (N.F. 33)
Desc(
Dr. Keylan discovered the Hypercube and led the foundational expedition into BR-000. Celebrated as DisCity’s savior, he died of illness and was memorialized with Keylan Square and Keylan University. However, Aesthia event parallels suggest Keylan may still be alive under a new identity)

entries.name: Character: Suspect R
entries.content:
Type: Sinner (Suspected), Shapeshifter
Name: Unknown (Possibly "Rebecca" or "S-[]")
Affiliation: Unknown
Status: At large
Desc(
A mysterious Sinner referred to as Suspect R, or "Rebecca" by some materials. She possesses shapeshifting abilities and has a personal connection to the Chief, claiming to have waited for them and calling them to “return” to her. She expresses hatred toward humanity and believes civilization is nearing collapse.
First appears during the Raid Minos incident, where she interrupts the Chief's consciousness repair, steals their bio-signature, and releases all MBCC prisoners. She is immune to Shackling, suggesting unique properties or origins.
She later disappears, telling the Chief she’ll be waiting “at the end” with answers—suggesting future confrontation. Public Security falsely reports sightings at SALVA; her true location remains unknown. Appears in the Creation crimebrand painting, implying symbolic or metaphysical relevance.)

Status: Deceased (N.F. 113)
Desc(
Commander of FAC’s elite anti-Black Ring unit, Squad N7. A hardened soldier known for his resilience, discipline, and leadership, 036 served as the vanguard in missions involving high-risk Mania exposure. Born N.F. 83.09.23, he died at age 29 during the BR-004 incident.
Fought and bested multiple Sinners in combat, including Nightmare and Earl, and provided critical support during the MBCC prison break and the Keylan Square crisis. Carried a personal photo collage of his fallen comrades, which he updated each time another squad member died.
During the final confrontation, he was mortally wounded and killed by the Chief while they were overwhelmed by Mania feedback from Zoya. With his dying act, he handed the Chief his last Hypercube to bring Chief back to their senses.)
